# src/editors/xrSdkControls/Controls/ColorPicker/ColorPicker.Designer.cs

> The picker's layout as data: four slider rows, a square swatch, and the size envelope that keeps it usable when docked.

**Needs** — [`ColorPicker.cs`](ColorPicker.cs.md) · [`ColorSampleBox.cs`](../ColorSampleBox.cs.md) · [`NumericSlider.cs`](../NumericSlider/NumericSlider.cs.md)
**Used by** — [`ColorPicker.cs`](ColorPicker.cs.md)
**Tier floor** — T4: a declarative layout description, generated by a visual designer and never hand-edited.

## Purpose

Machine-generated layout for [`ColorPicker`](ColorPicker.cs.md). It carries no behaviour, but it does carry numbers the behaviour assumes, which is why it is worth a page at all: a rebuild that redraws this panel by hand must reproduce the envelope, not the pixel offsets.

## State

```text
RECORD ColorPickerLayout
  rows        : 4 channel rows at a fixed vertical pitch, labelled R / G / B / A
  swatch      : square sample, right-aligned, anchored to the top-right corner
  toggle_row  : a "hexadecimal" checkbox below the channels
  hex_field   : an eight-character text field, present but hidden
  size        : fixed height; width stretches, with a floor wide enough for a usable slider
```

**Invariants** — every channel slider is configured identically: range 0 through 255, no decimal places, a fixed spinner width so the four numeric boxes line up, and a slider resolution finer than the value range so dragging can reach every integer. The alpha channel alone defaults to full, because a colour with no alpha authored is opaque.

## Notes

Three numbers are load-bearing and one is not.

**Load-bearing**: the channel range is 0–255 (the authored weather colours are stored as reals but presented as bytes, which is what an artist expects); the slider's internal resolution exceeds 255, so no integer value is unreachable by dragging; and the control declares both a minimum and a maximum size, because it lives in a resizable docked panel and a slider narrower than its own thumb is unusable.

**Not load-bearing**: the pixel coordinates. They are a designer artifact. A rebuild lays out four labelled rows and a swatch however its toolkit prefers.

One number could not be justified from the source: the vertical distance the hexadecimal toggle moves when the alpha row is hidden differs by one pixel from the pitch between channel rows. It looks like an off-by-one that nobody noticed rather than a decision.
